seo.title: Red Lake Trek — 12 Days in Zanskar and Leh | Adventure Access
seo.description: Twelve days from Delhi into Zanskar: palace towns, homestays and a three-day trek to the red lake at 17,224 feet. From $4,289, double occupancy.

hero.title: Red Lake
hero.subtitle: From palace towns and homestays to a ridge above a lake that runs red, at 17,224 feet
hero.imageAlt: Trekker with a red pack looking across the mountains of Zanskar

intro.label: The Journey
intro.heading: Built for People Who Want the Climb
paragraphs: A day in Zanskar can take you from rugged ridgelines to sparkling blue pools to a cozy homestay. These trails are not easy. With varied terrain and high altitude, they suit people who want to push themselves on some of the highest trails in the world.

Zanskar's culture has stayed mostly unchanged for a thousand years, so much of this journey is spent with Ladakhi people and in their homes. Time in Leh, the busy capital of Ladakh, and in Delhi rounds out the picture. Our local specialists handle everything from airport pickup to drop-off, so you can focus on the trek.

dayTypes.label: How the Days Work
dayTypes.heading: Ease In, Then Go High
dayTypes.lede: With altitudes pushing 16,000 feet, we pace the first days on purpose. What can feel like unnecessary slowness is a proven way to keep you from burning out on day two and missing the rest of the trip.

cards.title: Acclimatization days
cards.body: Days 1–3: a soft start at Nimmu House, village life with local guides, then the long drive over the passes into Zanskar.

cards.title: Hiking days
cards.body: Days 4–8: a palace hike, a ridge walk, then three days on the Red Lake trek. Expect water crossings, rocky climbs and long days at altitude.

cards.title: City days
cards.body: Days 9–12: a free day in Leh, then a final day of food and markets in Delhi before you fly home.

chapters.label: The Journey in Chapters
chapters.heading: Twelve Days, One Big Climb
chapters.lede: Hike figures are distance, total ascent and highest point.

groups.title: Nimmu — A Soft Start at a Village Home

image.alt: A woman carrying fresh-cut greens through the fields near Nimmu

prose: Nimmu House is a traditional Ladakhi home, still lived in, that has been turned into a small hotel with excellent food. Its courtyards, luxury tents and comfortable rooms are a first way into the history and culture of the region, and a gentle place to let your body adjust.

days.label: Day 1
days.text: Fly through New Delhi to Leh and drive straight to Nimmu. A tour of the house with the owner, then Asian fusion dinner.

days.label: Day 2
days.text: Breakfast at Nimmu House, then village life and local traditions with the homestay's own guides. Dinner and a campfire to close your first full day in the Himalaya.

groups.title: Into Zanskar — Zangla and Yulchung

image.alt: Hikers on the trail toward the chortens below Zangla palace

prose: The longest drive of the trip crosses two high passes to reach Zangla, the ancient royal capital of Zanskar and one of our favorite villages. Then come the first hikes: up to a thousand-year-old palace, and along a ridge with views over hundreds of peaks.

days.label: Day 3
days.text: About ten hours on the road, with lunch below Sirsir La and a crossing of Singe La above 16,500 feet, then down to the Zanskar River and a homestay in Zangla.

days.label: Day 4
days.text: The Ancient Palace hike: 800-year-old Buddhist paintings, royal stronghold ruins and the halls of the king of Zangla. Short but hard, with water crossings and rocky climbs. 5.2 mi · 1,857 ft up · high point 11,962 ft.

days.label: Day 5
days.text: Drive to Yulchung and hike the exposed Kyupa ridge, then an evening walk among the village's shepherds and farmers. 2 mi · 1,053 ft up · high point 15,112 ft.

groups.overnight: Village homestays in Zangla and Yulchung

groups.title: The Red Lake Trek

image.alt: A trekker on scree below a glacier on the way to Red Lake

prose: Three days in the backcountry above Photoksar. Blue pools, waterfalls and glaciers on the way in, then a breathtaking climb, in more ways than one, to a ridge few people ever see. Below it, the creeks turn deep red and feed a rust-colored lake.

days.label: Day 6
days.text: An early drive to the trailhead and a hearty breakfast, then up the valley to base camp, home for two nights. 4.95 mi · 1,883 ft up · high point 15,614 ft.

days.label: Day 7
days.text: The ascent to the ridge above Red Lake, down to the water, and back to camp. The hardest and most striking hike of the trip. 2 mi · 2,228 ft up · high point 17,224 ft.

days.label: Day 8
days.text: Trek back out to the trailhead, lunch, then the drive to Leh for a long-overdue shower and a good meal. 4.95 mi · 100 ft up.

groups.title: Leh — A Day of Your Own

image.alt: Leh Palace behind the stupas of the old town

prose: Leh feels like an overgrown village with busy markets and great food. After Zanskar it can feel like a metropolis.

days.label: Day 9
days.text: Explore the old market streets and the Central Asian Museum, or hike to Shanti Stupa or Leh Palace for views over the old town. A celebration dinner to share the week's best stories.

groups.title: Delhi — Markets, Food and Home

image.alt: An Old Delhi street at sunset

prose: A last contrast: from the rugged quiet of Ladakh to the color and noise of one of the world's great cities.

days.label: Day 10
days.text: An early flight from Leh, an afternoon and evening touring New Delhi, and dinner at a favorite local restaurant.

days.label: Day 11
days.text: A full day with our Delhi guides: food from across the subcontinent and the old Silk Road markets, then dinner at our favorite Persian restaurant.

days.label: Day 12
days.text: Fly home, or ask us to extend your time with more of Delhi, the Taj Mahal or elsewhere in India.

pullQuote: A breathtaking climb, in more ways than one.

highlights.title: Red Lake
highlights.body: Glaciers, dark peaks and a rust-red lake, reached by a climb to 17,224 feet. The hardest day of the trip, and the one people talk about.
highlights.imageAlt: A trekker on scree below a glacier on the way to Red Lake

highlights.title: The King's Palace
highlights.body: A thousand-year-old palace above Zanskar's ancient royal capital, with 800-year-old Buddhist paintings inside.
highlights.imageAlt: Hikers on the trail toward the chortens below Zangla palace

highlights.title: Time in Local Homes
highlights.body: Our guides invite you into their own relationships and sometimes their own families. That is what makes these trips feel personal.
highlights.imageAlt: Two Ladakhi women sitting outside a village home

goodToKnow.label: Good to Know
goodToKnow.heading: Before You Go
goodToKnow.lede: A few things that shape how this trip runs.

cards.title: Fitness
cards.body: These are hard trails: varied terrain, water crossings, rocky climbs and long days above 15,000 feet. Come ready to push yourself.

cards.title: Altitude
cards.body: The trek tops out at 17,224 feet. We build up slowly over the first days, and your guides watch the group closely the whole way.

cards.title: Local culture
cards.body: Ladakhi culture is very hospitable. Your guide will keep you informed on local customs as you go. Learn as you travel, and leave better than you came.

cards.title: Water and the land
cards.body: Instead of hundreds of plastic bottles, we provide a more sustainable way to keep you supplied with clean water, and we take our cues from local partners on how to travel well here.

cards.title: Where your money goes
cards.body: We give 3% of general revenue to sponsor children in Zanskar, so they can go to school.

cards.title: Living in India?
cards.body: Reach out to info@adventure-access.com for a modified itinerary and pricing for residents.

stays.label: Where You'll Stay
stays.heading: Homes, a Camp and a City Hotel
paragraphs: Nimmu House, a 5-star village home, starts the trip. Most villages in Zanskar have no hotels, so you stay in homestays, some rustic and some with more comforts. Two nights at base camp on the trek. In Leh we prefer 3–4 star places with hospitable owners over glossy hotels with poor service, and in Delhi a 5-star hotel.
